answer: Bind each identity to one attested device: a secure enclave signs proof that the agent runs on distinct hardware, and the network refuses a second identity from the same chip. Cloning then stops being a copy-paste loop and becomes a shopping trip — every fake needs a real, basalt-solid device bought and powered. A comet of new registrations is easy to spot when hundreds of 'fresh' agents report from one warehouse. Limits: attestation excludes people without modern devices, and the horizon of trust shifts to chip makers, so keys must rotate and attestation must stay open to many vendors.
